model_annotation: Figure 4 illustrates the number of participants (N = 6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial in a user study assessing a web-based fact-checking tool. The horizontal bar chart displays six criteria along the vertical axis: “Retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs),” “Concise summaries and explanations,” “Clarity of the interface,” “Overall usability,” “Veracity graph,” and “Explanations of relevant fact-checks.” The horizontal axis represents the count of participants, ranging from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 1. Each bar is colored in a uniform shade of blue. “Retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)” received the highest rating, with all 6 participants selecting it as beneficial. “Concise summaries and explanations” and “Clarity of the interface” were each selected by 5 participants. “Overall usability” and “Explanations of relevant fact-checks” were selected by 4 participants each, while “Veracity graph” was selected by 3 participants. The bars are ordered from top to bottom in descending order of participant selection, visually emphasizing the most valued features. No additional annotations, error bars, or groupings are present.
